# Fluncle libsql patch

This directory starts from the complete `libsql` 0.9.30 package published by crates.io. The downloaded `.crate` archive has SHA-256 `30fe980ac5693ed1f3db490559fb578885e913a018df64af8a1a46e1959a78df` and records upstream source commit `0653c5788d77ef16a97c56ff3e9fdc11717a72d9`. The archive contains 70 files and 625,890 logical bytes after extraction. `LICENSE.md` is the MIT license from that exact source commit; crates.io omitted the repository-root license from its package archive.

Fluncle changes only V2 response-body handling in `src/sync.rs` and `src/database/builder.rs`. Successful `/export/{generation}` chunks flow into the same-directory atomic temporary file before the existing flush-and-rename commit. A body error or cancelled export removes only that uniquely owned temporary file and never publishes it. Successful frame pulls are capped at the protocol's existing 128-frame request size, or 527,360 bytes, and JSON/error bodies—including a rejected initial `/info` protocol probe—are capped at 64 KiB before parsing or reporting. The native metadata format, hash, database-then-metadata ordering, one-sided-state rejection, authentication, generation selection, retry policy, and subsequent frame application are unchanged. The adjacent native tests require observable temp-file progress before response EOF, atomic publication after EOF, no destination or orphaned temporary file after a midstream body failure or cancellation, acceptance at the frame limit, and typed overflow errors that retain response status and context.
